name: wide_row_trig_chain
targeted_gap: seed sizes a wide [1,2048] contiguous inner tile from the byte model but leaves num_warps=4; a latency-bound transcendental chain in that fat tile cannot hide its latency with only 4 warps, while the default [32,32] keeps far more resident warps per SM.
hypothesis: bf16 traffic-2 (1 load + 1 store, bpe=4) -> seed [1,2048] at num_warps=4. Each of the 4 warps must serialize ~512 elements of a long sin/cos/tanh/exp/log chain; the SM holds too few resident warps to hide that latency. The default [32,32] spreads the same work over many small CTAs -> high resident-warp occupancy and full latency hiding. Measured seed 1.25-1.28x SLOWER than default across wide-N shapes.

name: skinny_m_wide_n_chain
targeted_gap: with tiny M and huge N the seed's [1,2048] tile makes the grid small (M * N/2048 programs) yet still 4 warps each; the SMs are left half-idle AND under-warped, while the default [32,32] launches many more programs.
hypothesis: A short-M, very-wide-N bf16 traffic-2 row still gets seed [1,2048] at num_warps=4. The grid (M * ceil(N/2048)) is small and each fat program has only 4 warps, so both grid occupancy and per-SM warp occupancy are starved on a latency-bound chain. The default [32,32] gives M/32-rounded-up * N/32 programs -- far more CTAs to fill the SMs. Expect seed >10% slower.

name: wide_row_moderate_chain
targeted_gap: even a MODERATE compute chain in the seed's [1,2048]/4-warp tile crosses the 10% regression bar; the byte model over-sizes the tile without ramping warps, so the boundary where 4 warps stop hiding latency is low.
hypothesis: bf16 traffic-2 with only a few transcendental ops still gets seed [1,2048] at num_warps=4. Even this lighter latency load exceeds what 4 warps on a 2048-wide tile can hide once the row is square-ish (2048x2048), where default [32,32] resident-warp occupancy wins. Measured ~1.10-1.13x slower -- shows the starvation bites well below a heavy chain, so the missing num_warps ramp is a broad gap.
